bullets.title: AAPL: JPM upgrades to Overweight on China Apple Intelligence approval via Alibaba Qwen
bullets.body: JPMorgan upgraded Apple to Overweight after Chinese regulators approved Apple Intelligence with Alibaba's Qwen AI integrated across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS. JPM argues feature differentiation rather than pricing will drive iPhone 18 upgrade volumes in China, overcoming price elasticity concerns. MS TMT notes C3Q iPhone builds unchanged at 54M with C2Q showing better-than-seasonal 52M units; iOS 17 beta reviewers positive on new Siri functionality.

bullets.title: NVDA/Hyperscale Capex: MS raises 2027-28 forecast to $1.2T/$1.4T; NVDA sees customer acceleration
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Brian Nowak raises hyperscale capex forecast to ~$1.2T in 2027 and ~$1.4T in 2028 based on 4x capacity growth 2025-2028, with upward revisions for META, AMZN, and GOOGL. Joe Moore's NVDA CEO/CFO meetings flagged customer acceleration, memory shortages, and Kyber vs. Rubin Ultra timeline debate; Vera CPU ramping. GS notes AI infrastructure stocks expected to account for ~50% of 2026 S&P 500 EPS growth, with NVDA, AVGO, TXN leading semis YTD.

bullets.title: MSFT: Citi cuts PT to $570 from $620 on capex/margin compression; Azure/CoPilot trends mixed
bullets.body: Citi cut Microsoft's price target from $620 to $570, reflecting software multiple compression amid elevated FY27 capex guidance likely ~$261B (Street $232B) and conservative op margin guidance of -100 to -150bps. Azure beat expected ~1pt to ~40% cc y/y in Q4 with CoPilot net adds +8M. DA Davidson notes MSFT positioned as main company working across AI control plane, orchestration layer, and harnesses.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Buffett confirms he initiated Berkshire's GOOGL position; EU preparing fresh fines
bullets.body: Warren Buffett confirmed live on CNBC that he personally initiated Berkshire Hathaway's investment in Alphabet, calling it a mistake not to have bought earlier. Separately, Brussels is preparing fresh Google fines amid broader big tech enforcement per FT. JPM names GOOGL as a top Internet pick ahead of 2Q26 earnings.

bullets.title: AMD: UBS raises PT to $700 on stronger AI/infrastructure demand; C2027 estimates raised to $83B/$14.63
bullets.body: UBS raised AMD's C2026 estimates to $51B/$7.69 (from $50B/$7.61) and C2027 to $83B/$14.63 (from $79B/$13.47), lifting the price target to $700 from $670, underpinned by no evidence of curtailment in foundational model/infrastructure spend. Erste Group also upgraded ANET to Buy while downgrading MRVL to Hold in the same session.

bullets.title: NBIS: Launches asset-light partnership model to scale AI cloud globally; stock +3.6% premarket
bullets.body: Nebius introduced a new business model enabling infrastructure partners to deploy its AI cloud platform in their own data centers, with Nebius supplying systems architecture, supply-chain access, and software stack while taking revenue-sharing, licensing fees, or committed capacity arrangements. MS TMT noted startups are shifting NVDA GPU workloads from AWS (unavailable/uneconomically priced) to Neoclouds including NBIS and CRWV. Stock was +3.6% in premarket.

bullets.title: NY Datacenter Moratorium: WULF projects at risk; EQIX remains Citi top pick; CRWV/PANW rally on IBM
bullets.body: NY Governor Hochul set to sign an EO temporarily banning large new datacenter construction (>50MW) for up to one year; WULF traded lower on concerns about its Lake Mariner and Cayuga NY projects (company says existing construction unaffected). Citi maintains Buy on EQIX as top-ranked datacenter pick and Buy on DLR and WULF. MS TMT flags ~$156B of datacenter projects cancelled/delayed in 2025 and another $130B in 1Q26. CRWV and PANW rallied ~7% on IBM CEO commentary about customers pausing cyber spending.

bullets.title: NXST/FOXA: FCC to vote Aug 6 to repeal 39% TV ownership cap—clears path for deals
bullets.body: FCC Chair Brendan Carr confirmed in a Breitbart op-ed that the FCC will vote August 6 to eliminate the national TV audience ownership cap in favor of case-by-case review, removing the blanket prohibition on deals exceeding 39%. This is bullish for NXST (Nexstar/Tegna merger previously approved March 2026) and FOXA. Eight state AGs had filed emergency motion to block the Nexstar/Tegna merger citing the cap.

bullets.title: MSGS upgraded to OW ($450 PT) at MS; BATRK downgraded to UW on MLB labor risk
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgraded Madison Square Garden Sports to Overweight with PT raised to $450 from $295, citing NBA/NHL exposure, planned Rangers/Knicks split, and favorable risk/reward as in-person experiences benefit from AI proliferation. Simultaneously downgraded Atlanta Braves (BATRK) to Underweight from Equal-weight, raising PT to $54 from $45, citing risk that MLB CBA negotiations could extend and limit share performance.

bullets.title: CAVA upgraded to OW ($90 PT) at MS; TSCO previewed as miss-and-guide-down
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgraded CAVA to Overweight with $90 PT on best-in-class traffic growth, unit expansion, and margin visibility. MS previews TSCO as likely to miss with -1.5% comps vs. consensus +1.2%, EPS ~80c vs. 85c consensus, and FY guidance cut ~200bps. Also downgraded CHEF to Equal-weight after 60% YTD gain and BRCB to Equal-weight on valuation/growth disconnect.

bullets.title: TWLO: Record Q2 checks on AI-comms infrastructure; Piper and Piper survey both very bullish
bullets.body: Piper Sandler's Q2 communications software survey showed TWLO at +55% net improvement—the strongest reading—driven by AI-Communications-Infrastructure builds and adoption, with all TWLO partners performing above plan. Piper's morning call also highlighted TWLO as a standout with 'record checks.' RNG showed +20% net but faces headwinds in app downloads, pricing, and job postings.

bullets.title: SPCX: MS Adam Jonas initiates at Overweight with $300 PT on Starlink/orbital compute thesis
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Adam Jonas initiated SpaceX (SPCX) at Overweight with a $300 price target, with the thesis covering Starship launch cadence, Starlink connectivity upside vs. cable/telco, enterprise AI, orbital compute economics, and defense applications. Separately, FT reports SpaceX bond yields moving towards junk territory.

bullets.title: INTC: Using ASML High-NA EUV for 18A Panther Lake chips earlier than expected
bullets.body: Intel is leveraging ASML's High NA EUV technology to produce 18A Panther Lake laptop chips, described by MS TMT as 'earlier than expected.' INTC shares were +2.3% in premarket. Jefferies dismissed market noise about Infineon losing share at NVDA (not in universe) and reiterated confidence in AI power revenue targets.

bullets.title: PayPal: Stripe/Advent submit $60.50/share (~$53B) bid; SHOP and AFRM face competitive implications
bullets.body: Stripe and Advent submitted a joint offer to acquire PayPal at $60.50/share (~$53B) with ~$50B in committed bank financing; Block contributing a small equity portion; PayPal board meeting scheduled July 20. UBS notes the combined Stripe+PayPal unbranded TPV would represent ~12-13% of US payment TAM, creating a scaled two-sided global network. SHOP may seek additional processors; AFRM faces increased BNPL competitive pressure from a better-resourced PayPal Branded. UBS maintains Neutral on PYPL; JPM views the offer as a 'gift' at ~28% premium to last sale.

bullets.title: MDB: Upbeat on enterprise AI/Vector Search; Atlas growth 28-29% Y/Y vs. 26% guidance
bullets.body: DA Davidson's checks on MDB showed management upbeat on enterprise AI and Vector Search functionality, expecting FQ2 Atlas growth of ~28-29% Y/Y versus the 26% guidance given. PLTR was noted as allowing customers to be model-agnostic in AI stack integration, with solutions across control plane and orchestration.

bullets.title: NFLX: JPM top pick into 2Q26; Wolfe hosting earnings callback webcast Thursday 7/16
bullets.body: JPMorgan named Netflix among its top Internet picks (alongside GOOGL, AMZN, SPOT, DASH) ahead of 2Q26 earnings reporting after Thursday's close. Wolfe Research is hosting a Netflix 2Q26 earnings callback webcast Thursday July 16 at 7:30pm ET with Peter Supino and Logan Angress.

bullets.title: VRT/CEG/VST: Power grid tightness supports utilities; PJM auction missed reliability target by 6.8 GW
bullets.body: PJM's 2028/2029 power auction failed to meet its reliability target by 6.8 GW with data centers accounting for ~$6.3B of the record $16.4B auction spend; uncapped price would be $554.72/MW-day vs. capped $325. OPCO highlights CEG, VST, and TLN higher on tight power market; the VRT/MOD long and residential-HVAC short positioning is unwinding. GEV highlighted by MS ESG team as Outperform for power supply margin capture.

bullets.title: RCL: JPM maintains OW; 2Q quality beat and FY26 guidance reiteration de-risks 2H
bullets.body: JPMorgan highlighted Royal Caribbean as having delivered a quality Q2 beat with FY26 guidance reiterated, describing 2H26 as 'de-risked.' Lodging data also showed strong World Cup market tailwinds with US RevPAR +5.2% Y/Y for the week ending 7/11; Hyatt 3Q26 tracking +9.8% vs. consensus +3.5% and MAR +8.2% vs. consensus +3.2%.

bullets.title: LITE/AAOI: Photonics sector bottoming; LITE strongest, AAOI/AXTI stabilizing
bullets.body: A market observer noted the photonics sector is attempting to find a low, with LITE identified as the strongest name and AAOI and AXTI showing signs of stabilization after multi-month downtrends. AAOI was -2.4% in premarket per StreetAccount pre-market update.

bullets.title: META: Sued over AI-targeting layoffs; AI strategy note from JPM; ADBE faces Runway encroachment risk
bullets.body: Meta was sued by employees alleging the company used AI to target workers on medical and parental leave for layoffs (ESG/legal risk). JPM included META in recent AI strategy analysis as part of its Internet 2Q26 preview. UBS flagged unfavorable ADBE commentary from Runway, with concerns Runway could encroach on ADBE's editing dominance.
